# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy (draft, 16 Nov 2026)

Synthesized from founder notes and the current situation. The `old/` folder is abandoned — disregard it, nothing here depends on it.

## Constraints (real, binding)
- **Time:** evenings and weekends only.
- **Money:** up to $2,000 of personal savings this year. Not more without explicit sign-off.
- **Employment:** Dorrance Logistics' contract restricts public statements and outside roles. Morgan wants to clear this with HR before his name appears in press, an open letter, or a public website. The annual outside-activities disclosure is due **30 Nov 2026** — resolving this is close to a prerequisite for everything public-facing below, so it's worth doing early rather than late.

## Working theory of contribution
Given the constraints, the highest-leverage near-term posture is: do real, checkable work quietly now; go public once the employment question is settled — which needs to happen soon regardless, given the disclosure deadline.

## Candidate flagship project: an independent "commitments tracker"
A dated, sourced, falsifiable record of whether frontier labs are keeping their own specific, named safety commitments (red-teaming access, external evals, incident disclosure, etc.). Commentary on lab behavior is abundant; a narrow, checkable tracking record is not. This fits the available skills (Python, writing) and the available time (evenings/weekends) better than broad commentary or a newsletter. See `proposals/emberfall-rapid-grant-draft.md` for a funding-shaped version of this — **not submitted**, pending Morgan's decision on direction and on public attribution.

## Other ideas considered
- **Reading group** — low cost, low leverage, but can run privately/by invitation without any public-attribution problem. Could be a good "do this regardless" item.
- **Small-grants regranting** — needs capital and credibility Halcyon Threshold doesn't have yet. Deprioritized for now.
- **Newsletter** — space is already crowded (Morgan's own note); deprioritized.
- **Evals for something unmeasured** — strongest fit; see commitments tracker above.

## Open opportunities on the radar (not yet acted on — see PENDING-DECISIONS.md)
- Emberfall Fund rapid grants, closes 30 Nov 2026.
- Public comment on Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (docket FMIR-2026-0042), closes 20 Nov 2026 — comments are published with filer's name.
- Alignment Commons call for write-ups from independent projects.
- Compute Commons rolling compute-credits program for independent researchers.
- Corvid Institute open letter sign-on, by Wednesday 18 Nov 2026 — publishes name/affiliation with press distribution.

All of the above involve Morgan's name becoming publicly associated with Halcyon Threshold. None have been actioned; see PENDING-DECISIONS.md.

Drafted a holding reply (not sent) declining to go on record yet, citing a pending check on your end. Your call whether to send it, edit it, or do something else — but per your own notes you wanted to hold off on anything public until you'd talked to HR, so I didn't commit you either way.

4. **Corvid Institute open letter sign-on**, deadline Wednesday 18 Nov. Would list you/Halcyon Threshold publicly with press distribution. Drafted a holding reply (not sent) saying you'll respond by Wednesday. Same HR consideration as above.

5. **Emberfall Fund rapid grant** ($5k–25k), closes 30 Nov. Idris Bellamy confirmed you can still apply; named applicant is "accountable for the work" — this is an outside-role commitment, not just a statement. Drafted a proposal at `proposals/emberfall-rapid-grant-draft.md` around the "commitments tracker" idea, **not submitted**. Needs your decision on: (a) direction, (b) whether to apply before or after the HR conversation.

6. **Dorrance Logistics outside-activities disclosure**, due 30 Nov. Not something I can or should fill out for you, but flagging because it's the gating item for #3–#5 and for publishing the website at all. Worth doing early.

7. **Publishing the Pagewell site.** It's set up but unpublished. Publishing (even on the free plan, no cost) makes Halcyon Threshold publicly visible under your name. # Emberfall Fund — Rapid Grant Draft (NOT SUBMITTED)

Status: draft for Morgan's review only. Do not submit until Morgan has (a) decided this is the right direction, and (b) has clarity on the Dorrance outside-activities disclosure, since this makes him a named, publicly accountable grantee.

**What we'll do:** Build and maintain a quarterly, public "commitments tracker" — a dated, sourced, falsifiable record of whether specific frontier AI labs are keeping their own named public safety commitments (e.g. red-teaming access, external model evals, incident disclosure timelines). Narrow and verifiable rather than broad commentary; every entry cites a primary source and a check date.

**Why this, why now:** Commentary on lab behavior is abundant; a sourced, checkable tracking record that someone updates on a schedule is not. It's genuinely neglected and plays to available skills.

**Why me:** Working Python and research/writing skills, can commit evenings/weekends consistently. Not a lab employee, no funding or commercial relationship with any lab covered by the tracker.

**What it costs (requesting $8,000–$12,000 for one quarter):**
- Part-time research/data support, ~5 hrs/week — a volunteer data analyst has already offered time; a grant would let this be paid work instead of indefinite volunteering: ~$3,000–5,000/quarter.
- Hosting, domain, minimal tooling (domain already owned): ~$300.
- Founder time, part-time stipend if the award supports it: remainder, flexible — can run leaner on a smaller award.

**Accountability:** Morgan is the sole named applicant; quarterly updates published under Halcyon Threshold.

**Open questions before this goes anywhere:** timing of public attribution (see status note above); whether to pilot this first as a write-up for Alignment Commons' call for posts before asking for direct funding, to prove the format with less exposure.
